a.text: The wandering singer closes the bulky box and carries it on her back again.
She takes one step and then another. The pile of limbs and coagulated fluids beneath her feet instantly rot and weather away.
On her third step, as the hems of her dress flutter in the sea breeze, the tiny particles of crystal scattered all across the ground disperse into the air as well.

steps.name: Inquisitor
steps.text: D-Did you see that just now?

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: I saw all of it.

steps.name: Inquisitor
steps.text: How did she even do that?

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: She is a singer...

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: Inquisitor, this is nothing strange for her. That's something she's always been capable of.

steps.name: Inquisitor
steps.text: Singer... what? You're still calling her by that name?

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: How else should I call her? You're the Inquisitor. You tell me.

steps.name: Inquisitor
steps.text: I need to go outside.

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: Hey, wait!

steps.name: Inquisitor
steps.text: What are you doing? So you think you can stop me too? I am an Inquisitor!

steps.name: Inquisitor
steps.text: What is this... So slimy...

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: Phew... I-I got it! I landed a blow! That was close, Inquisitor.

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: Thank goodness you smashed this chair to pieces. It gave me a weapon when I needed one to smack this thing. It would've climbed on top of you otherwise!

steps.name: Inquisitor
steps.text: Y-You...! All of you are out of your minds!

steps.name: Inquisitor
steps.text: How could you not be scared, seeing these things?

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: I was. Just a little. They're not as scary as you, though.

steps.name: Inquisitor
steps.text: You... How dare you compare me to these monsters?!

steps.name: Inquisitor
steps.text: Fine, I won't argue with you. You haven't seen them before, and you have no idea what they are capable of. It's no wonder you are not scared.

steps.name: Inquisitor
steps.text: Wait, the other inhabitants are coming outside. They... What are they doing?!

steps.name: Inquisitor
steps.text: They're not scared at all either...

steps.name: Inquisitor
steps.text: The problem...

steps.name: Inquisitor
steps.text: I need to find where this problem lies...

a.text: The problem, as the Inquisitor sees it, is the most abnormal sight she sees unfolding before her eyes.
The Inquisitor looks at the girl standing before her. Then, she looks over at the lone Ægir standing outside.
Finally, she turns her gaze to the inhabitants now lining into the streets.

steps.name: Male Inhabitant D
steps.text: Sand.

steps.name: Male Inhabitant C
steps.text: Salt... So salty.

steps.name: Male Inhabitant D
steps.text: That thing just now. You can eat it. It's gone. A shame.

steps.name: Male Inhabitant C
steps.text: Too bad.

steps.name: Male Inhabitant D
steps.text: You can eat salt.

steps.name: Male Inhabitant C
steps.text: Yes, it's edible.

steps.name: Male Inhabitant D
steps.text: More. More... Mhmm, blurgh.

steps.name: Male Inhabitant C
steps.text: It's dirty.

steps.name: Male Inhabitant D
steps.text: Swallow it. More...

steps.name: Inquisitor
steps.text: Stop right there!

steps.name: Inquisitor
steps.text: I still have questions for you, and you will answer them—What do you mean, they're here for you?

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: I'm bleeding.

steps.name: Inquisitor
steps.text: I can tell that much. You were wounded in your fight with the High Inquisitor, so you ran away. How's that got anything to do with these... monsters showing up?

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: They can smell my blood.

steps.name: Inquisitor
steps.text: They're here to... kill you? I saw them all dashing toward you—

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: Perhaps.

steps.name: Inquisitor
steps.text: Perhaps?

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: They can't hurt me.

steps.name: Inquisitor
steps.text: Y-You! Do you know how annoying the way you talk is?

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: It's the truth.

steps.name: Inquisitor
steps.text: They—I mean these monsters—They're gone.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: Yes.

steps.name: Inquisitor
steps.text: They're all gone without a trace, as if they never were. If I didn't see them clearly with my own eyes, I would've thought this all a dream.

steps.name: Inquisitor
steps.text: These monsters... the Sea Terrors. I've come across them plenty of times before. They don't look that much like these ones, but they have that same disgusting stench.

steps.name: Inquisitor
steps.text: But that was on the beach, and they never show up in such numbers. Do you mean to tell me they do not actually live in the sea?

steps.name: Inquisitor
steps.text: They only show up when someone goes look for trouble at the shore, right? Just like what you were doing during the day.

steps.name: Inquisitor
steps.text: And now they came this far away from the beach. They've nearly made it to the streets.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: They can make it far more places than you can imagine. They can spread by changing form, permeating every corner of the world.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: Be it iron-forged cities, villages built atop the highlands, or barrenlands with nothing but sand. Wherever one can go, they can too.

steps.name: Inquisitor
steps.text: How is that possible?!

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: The world is surrounded by ocean. Just because you cannot see the ocean does not mean that the land where you stand will forever remain untouched by its waters. The seas are alive and ever flowing, and so are the calamities they bring with them.

steps.name: Inquisitor
steps.text: I know there are places where the seas are dangerous, but I didn't know that the danger existed... in the lands outside Iberia too.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: Danger exists everywhere.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: Still, these calamities are here because of me. If you come any closer, you will be affected too.

steps.name: Inquisitor
steps.text: You... Just who are you?!

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: I already told you.

steps.name: Inquisitor
steps.text: Enough with the wandering singer thing! I saw it all.

steps.name: Inquisitor
steps.text: You were fighting them, and you know exactly how to fight them too.

steps.name: Inquisitor
steps.text: When you finished them off, your technique was so much better than when you were fighting the High Inquisitor and me.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: I don't have quite the same handle on fighting humans.

steps.name: Inquisitor
steps.text: A-Ahem... Let's dispense with the strange talk... I know you are a strange one, but still...

steps.name: Inquisitor
steps.text: Were you... a hunter? I can kind of see that in your eyes.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: If you think I am, then sure.

steps.name: Inquisitor
steps.text: And you hunted these... Sea Terrors before?

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: They need to be eliminated.

steps.name: Inquisitor
steps.text: Ugh... The way you talk just grates me so much, but—I don't even know why—coming from you, this doesn't sound like a lie at all.

steps.name: Inquisitor
steps.text: Singer, hunter... It doesn't matter to me what you were.

steps.name: Inquisitor
steps.text: Going by the circumstances, I suppose you saved not just my life, but everyone who lives on this street, maybe even the entire town.

steps.name: Inquisitor
steps.text: You may be the enemy of my enemy, but that does not make you a friend.

steps.name: Inquisitor
steps.text: No matter the case, I need to do my job. I have to take you away.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: You were asking me what I am doing here.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: I am here to seek an answer, and this answer only has to do with me... and the person I am looking for.

steps.name: Inquisitor
steps.text: You wouldn't tell me a thing earlier.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: You didn't give me a chance to tell you.

steps.name: Inquisitor
steps.text: You may have given me an answer now, but that doesn't mean my judgment has changed.

steps.name: Inquisitor
steps.text: You don't belong to this city. A person like you showing up is a mistake.

steps.name: Inquisitor
steps.text: Not to mention... You told me yourself you brought this disaster with you.

steps.name: Inquisitor
steps.text: —It's certainly not how I imagined it, though.

steps.name: Inquisitor
steps.text: Nonetheless, Ægir. You are dangerous. You are a danger to this city. At the same time, this city is also a danger to you.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: Hm?

steps.name: Inquisitor
steps.text: Look at them. They are... eating scraps of the Sea Terrors' remains. They don't fear these monsters... No, they don't even know what monsters are.

steps.name: Inquisitor
steps.text: They feed when they are hungry. As a monster does. And humans... humans know what fear is.

steps.name: Inquisitor
steps.text: So... Are they still human?

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: All I know is that they're trying their best to live.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: From that perspective, there's nothing that sets humans and monsters apart.

steps.name: Inquisitor
steps.text: When they live like that... can you really say they are alive?

steps.name: Inquisitor
steps.text: The High Inquisitor told me to see it for myself, and only now do I understand what he meant.

steps.name: Inquisitor
steps.text: In this city, the biggest problem isn't whatever its citizens are doing. It's that they are still alive in this manner—This is the most abnormal thing of all.

steps.name: Inquisitor
steps.text: Like you, they are dangerous, and this danger must be kept under control, just like how mistakes must be corrected.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: You haven't given up.

steps.name: Inquisitor
steps.text: Now I really can't let you go.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: I already told you. I still have something to take care of, and I am in a hurry.

steps.name: Inquisitor
steps.text: Looks like we will have to do this again, then.

steps.name: Inquisitor
steps.text: Ægir, I know you are hurt, and you must be exhausted after fighting the Sea Terrors.

steps.name: Inquisitor
steps.text: But I will not go easy on you.

steps.name: Inquisitor
steps.text: What's this? A small shell?

steps.name: Inquisitor
steps.text: It wasn't you, Ægir... You wouldn't throw this at me.

steps.name: Inquisitor
steps.text: Perhaps one of the locals vomiting their guts out on the floor? No, it can't be them. They don't even know what it is they are stuffing into their mouths. They wouldn't move against me.

steps.name: Inquisitor
steps.text: Is it... from the window over to the side?

steps.name: Inquisitor
steps.text: Who is it?!

steps.name: Inquisitor
steps.text: Who threw this? Step forward!

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: Hahh...

steps.name: Inquisitor
steps.text: You? Did you throw this at me? Are you still trying to get in my way, to protect this Ægir?

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: Uh, yes! It's me!

steps.name: Old Inhabitant
steps.text: Anita, stop it with your nonsense.

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: Grandma Petra?! Y-You should stay inside...

steps.name: Old Inhabitant
steps.text: I did it, Your Honor.

steps.name: Inquisitor
steps.text: Did you just call me 'Your Honor?'

steps.name: Old Inhabitant
steps.text: I know who exactly you are. These ones know nothing.

steps.name: Inquisitor
steps.text: There's someone still sane here...?

steps.name: Inquisitor
steps.text: Old woman, perhaps your eyes aren't as good as they used to be. Please step back. We are taking care of something dangerous here.

steps.name: Old Inhabitant
steps.text: Look, Your Honor. My eyes are as perfect as they can be. Even if the sky's pitch black, I will have no trouble hitting you as long as you forget to dodge.

steps.name: Old Inhabitant
steps.text: Oh, tiny seashells, beautiful waves♪

steps.name: Old Inhabitant
steps.text: One shell after another, one beating wave after another...

steps.name: Inquisitor
steps.text: You admitted it yourself. Now I must—

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: Inquisitor... Your Honor! Grandma Petra's sick... Please don't blame her?

steps.name: Inquisitor
steps.text: She's sick? No wonder. Yes, I can see that.

steps.name: Old Inhabitant
steps.text: Oh, Little Anita. Enough nonsense. How am I sick?

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: Grandma Petra, please stop. Please.

steps.name: Old Inhabitant
steps.text: Sick... sick!

steps.name: Old Inhabitant
steps.text: What's sick is Sal Viento itself! Yes—This place, and all its people! And you, almighty Inquisitor... You are sick as well!

steps.name: Inquisitor
steps.text: You, take your senile grandmother home.

steps.name: Inquisitor
steps.text: I have more important things to deal with.

steps.name: Old Inhabitant
steps.text: What important things? What's more important than being alive?

steps.name: Inquisitor
steps.text: As an Inquisitor, there are things that I have to safeguard even with my life. For example, all the things that the law says are correct... as well as our country itself.

steps.name: Old Inhabitant
steps.text: You will use your life... to safeguard whose life?

steps.name: Inquisitor
steps.text: I... Whatever... I shouldn't waste any more of my time with you. Your old age and your illness have done a number on your faculties, citizen. I can overlook your crazy behavior so long as you stand aside and let me take care of what's important.

steps.name: Old Inhabitant
steps.text: Your Honor, I'm afraid I don't understand this right or wrong, this country of yours.

steps.name: Old Inhabitant
steps.text: I just want to ask you this. This thing you are trying to uphold. We were never part of it, isn't that right?

steps.name: Inquisitor
steps.text: What...?!

steps.name: Old Inhabitant
steps.text: You Inquisitors took our people away. You said they were disrupting order, that they assaulted someone while they were stealing food. They just wanted to live.

steps.name: Inquisitor
steps.text: That wasn't me... but if they committed a crime, then that's how it should be.

steps.name: Old Inhabitant
steps.text: And they've never been back.

steps.name: Old Inhabitant
steps.text: You brought your bad guys away, but did that improve our lives?

steps.name: Inquisitor
steps.text: When you remove all the factors that bring chaos to society in time, there will naturally be order.

steps.name: Old Inhabitant
steps.text: Yet there is less and less food to go by... Those of us who got on in years either die of hunger or disease. Even some of our young couldn't endure.

steps.name: Old Inhabitant
steps.text: You speak of order... but all you want is for us to die quietly, isn't it? That way, there will be no more noise, and you upper class folks can finally lie down on your fluffy beds for a quiet night of sleep.

steps.name: Inquisitor
steps.text: That's not it.

steps.name: Inquisitor
steps.text: All of Iberia is suffering. Not just you.

steps.name: Inquisitor
steps.text: Shouldn't a criminal who steals resources and harms the people be stopped? Suppose there are ten meals before us. They should feed ten Iberians.

steps.name: Inquisitor
steps.text: If no one is there to tell them how much they should get, they will fight to no end. In the end, only one of the ten will remain.

steps.name: Inquisitor
steps.text: The Inquisition draws the boundary of right and wrong amid this chaos and guides the masses to the right path. Otherwise the whole country would've long become a heap of sand.

steps.name: Old Inhabitant
steps.text: Everything you said... I don't get it, and it's nothing I can see.

steps.name: Old Inhabitant
steps.text: We don't have a way out. When we truly wanted one, where were you?

steps.name: Inquisitor
steps.text: I... I want to help you. I am working hard to become a full-fledged Inquisitor. I took this path because I want to help the people, and I trust that this is the only way.

steps.name: Old Inhabitant
steps.text: Help us...?

steps.name: Old Inhabitant
steps.text: I hoped, imagined, thirsted, even dreamt of someone coming to save us. I screamed through so many nights till my throat was hoarse.

steps.name: Old Inhabitant
steps.text: You never came.

steps.name: Old Inhabitant
steps.text: Will you Inquisitors only come when someone has done something wrong?

steps.name: Old Inhabitant
steps.text: Look at these old bones. I never imagined I'd live this long. What a tragedy. Every day is filled with nothing but pain.

steps.name: Old Inhabitant
steps.text: Look, I'm attacking you, Your Honor.

steps.name: Old Inhabitant
steps.text: Take me away! Take me, and end me! Put me out of my misery!

steps.name: Old Inhabitant
steps.text: Hurry, do it! I can't wait no longer—I've waited all these years! *Cough* *cough*...

steps.name: Inquisitor
steps.text: I don't want to fight you. Your anger... is understandable. My sword should not...

steps.name: Inquisitor
steps.text: Don't force my hand, citizen.

steps.name: Old Inhabitant
steps.text: *Cough* *Cough*...

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: Grandma!

steps.name: Old Inhabitant
steps.text: Oh... Anita... You came to the plaza too.

steps.name: Old Inhabitant
steps.text: It's dark... Why is there no singing yet?

steps.name: Old Inhabitant
steps.text: Singer, you said you are a singer. Why aren't you singing? Where is your harp? I want to dance. I need a tune.

steps.name: Old Inhabitant
steps.text: Look, Your Honor. You're more useless than a wandering singer. She sings for us. She's even brave enough... to stand in front of the rest of us.

steps.name: Old Inhabitant
steps.text: I'm not scared of monsters, and I'm not scared of death. What I am scared of is this life. Am I crazy, Anita?

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: Grandma, it's okay. You're shaking. It's cold here. Why don't we go back? Lie down and get some rest. You'll feel better.

steps.name: Old Inhabitant
steps.text: Okay... Okay. Let's go. We'll go home. It isn't like I know where else to go anyway.

steps.name: Inquisitor
steps.text: You...!

steps.name: Old Inhabitant
steps.text: Did you change your mind? If you changed your mind, you can still take me away. That, or kill me. At the very least... I would get to die like a person.

steps.name: Old Inhabitant
steps.text: Do it while I'm still alive, Your Honor. I don't have much time left.

steps.name: Old Inhabitant
steps.text: Come, let's go... Singer, come with us. I want to hear you sing.

steps.name: Inquisitor
steps.text: I will let you go... for now.

steps.name: Inquisitor
steps.text: But I will be back!

steps.name: Inquisitor
steps.text: And you, Ægir! I'm watching you, and I will get to the end of this! Don't think you can get out of this one!

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: Phew... That was close.

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: Singer, are you okay? You look white as a sheet.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: I'm fine.

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: You don't need to act so tough anymore. The Inquisitor is gone.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: I'm not afraid of her.

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: I know. I can tell you aren't afraid. What would someone like you be afraid of?

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: She's not a bad person.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: And it would be a good thing for you if I leave this place.

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: A good thing? There's nothing good here.

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: Grandma might've said all that, but she doesn't really hate the Inquisitor. She hates something else. I know it.

steps.name: Old Inhabitant
steps.text: Now dance. Haha, I love your singing...

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: Stop spinning around, Grandma. You're tired. The singer will sing for you. Isn't that right?

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: Give me your hand, singer. Let me take a look at your wound.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: No...

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: I can't come near you because it's dangerous, right?

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: It's okay. I trust you. If anything happens, you will win.

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: Look, your wounds aren't so bad at all. No more bleeding.

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: Singer, you are amazing. You heal up so quickly.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: It could've been quicker.

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: But even so, you don't look well to me, and the house you picked was blown to pieces. I doubt even you can get a good sleep there now. Why don't you come home with me and Grandma Petra?

steps.name: Old Inhabitant
steps.text: That's right. Stay with us. Don't let them come look for any more trouble with you.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: No...

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: Okay, enough 'No's, 'No need's, and 'I have other things to do.' I am sick of them.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: I can still...

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: Ugh...

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: Look at you. Out of strength, no? You need someone to look after you, and you definitely need some sleep.

steps.name: Anita
steps.text: I also think the person you're looking for probably doesn't want to see you pushing yourself like this.

steps.name: Male Inhabitant A
steps.text: What was that... just now?

steps.name: Male Inhabitant A
steps.text: None of my business anymore...

steps.name: Male Inhabitant A
steps.text: I shouldn't ask questions. I have my answer now. I know the way. I know where to go.

steps.name: Male Inhabitant A
steps.text: I need to go straight... Straight ahead.

steps.name: Male Inhabitant A
steps.text: Tomorrow, everyone will have food to eat. I... No, we... All of us will get to live.

steps.name: Male Inhabitant A
steps.text: 'We want to survive, so we must love one another even more.'

steps.name: Male Inhabitant A
steps.text: 'For love is the inseparable bond between us.'

steps.name: Male Inhabitant A
steps.text: 'I will become stronger.'

steps.name: Male Inhabitant A
steps.text: 'Our people will likewise become stronger.'

a.text: The man limps forward toward the pitch-black seas until he comes upon an object blocking his way.

steps.name: Male Inhabitant A
steps.text: This...

steps.name: Male Inhabitant A
steps.text: Her harp. It's here.

steps.name: Male Inhabitant A
steps.text: (Tries to play the harp like Skadi does)

steps.name: Male Inhabitant A
steps.text: (Chords)

steps.name: Male Inhabitant A
steps.text: Sounds horrible.

steps.name: Male Inhabitant A
steps.text: This is useless. I will leave it here to rot.
